{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded Day 1 visits with multiple procedures",
      "quote": "Day 1 (Day 1) | Day 8 ±3 (Day 8) | Day 29 ±3 (Day 29) | Day 50 ±3 (Day 50) | Day 1 ±3 (Day 1) | Day 22 ±3 (Day 22) | Day 43 ±3 (Day 43) | Day 1 ±3 (Day 1) | Day 22 ±3 (Day 22) | Day 43 ±3 (Day 43) | Day 64 ±3 (Day 64) | EOT Visit4,5 30 days after last dose ±7 days | Safety Follow-up4,5 90 days after last dose ±10 days | Tumor Assessment Every 4 months (±10 days) | Survival Follow-up4,5 Every 4 months (±10 days)",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The schedule shows multiple visits labeled 'Day 1' (three separate Day 1 columns) and repeated cycles, but the table is confusing and likely overloads patients with frequent visits and procedures, especially on Day 1 where cemiplimab, ISA101b, PK, ADA, biomarkers, and physical exams are all scheduled.",
      "fix": "Clarify the visit structure (e.g., cycle/day numbering) and consider consolidating procedures or extending windows to reduce patient burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Frequent tumor assessments every 4 months may be burdensome",
      "quote": "Tumor Assessment Every 4 months (±10 days)",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Tumor assessments every 4 months with a 10-day window may be frequent for patients on long-term follow-up, especially if they are stable, and could be extended to every 6 months to reduce burden.",
      "fix": "Consider extending tumor assessment frequency to every 6 months for patients in long-term follow-up."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs every hour during 4-hour observation period is burdensome",
      "quote": "Vital signs will also be taken every hour during the 4-hour observation period following ISA101b administration.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "9.2.3.4 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring vital signs every hour for 4 hours after ISA101b administration adds significant patient burden and staff time, especially on days with many other procedures.",
      "fix": "Reduce frequency to every 2 hours or only as clinically indicated, or shorten observation period if safety data support it."
    },
    {
      "title": "PBMC collection optional but scheduled at many visits",
      "quote": "T cell immune monitoring PBMC sample |  | X | X | X |  | X |  |  | X |  |  |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PBMC collection is optional but appears at multiple visits (Day 1, 8, 29, 50, and EOT), which may be burdensome for patients who consent, and the optional nature may lead to inconsistent data.",
      "fix": "Limit PBMC collection to fewer key timepoints (e.g., baseline and EOT) to reduce burden and improve consistency."
    },
    {
      "title": "PK and ADA samples for cemiplimab collected at multiple visits",
      "quote": "PK sample (cemiplimab) |  | X |  |  |  | X |  |  | X |  |  |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PK and ADA samples are collected at Day 1, 29, 50, and EOT, which is frequent and may be burdensome; consider reducing to sparse sampling if PK model supports it.",
      "fix": "Evaluate if PK/ADA sampling can be reduced to fewer visits without compromising objectives."
    },
    {
      "title": "Soluble biomarkers collected at multiple visits with no clear rationale",
      "quote": "Soluble biomarkers (serum) |  | X | X | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Soluble biomarkers are collected at Day 1, 8, 29, and EOT, adding burden; if exploratory, consider reducing frequency to key timepoints.",
      "fix": "Reduce soluble biomarker collection to baseline and EOT or other critical timepoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse events only collected at safety follow-up, not at treatment visits",
      "quote": "Adverse events |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The schedule shows adverse events only at the Safety Follow-up visit, but AEs should be collected at every visit during the study. This is a critical omission that could lead to missing safety data.",
      "fix": "Add adverse event collection to all visits from Day 1 through EOT and follow-up."
    },
    {
      "title": "Electrocardiogram only at screening and EOT, not during treatment",
      "quote": "Electrocardiogram | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X |  |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "ECG is only at screening and EOT, but cemiplimab can cause QT prolongation; more frequent ECGs may be needed during treatment to monitor cardiac safety.",
      "fix": "Add ECGs at key treatment visits (e.g., Cycle 1 Day 1 and subsequent cycles) to monitor QT interval."
    }
  ]
}
